key_insight: SELDON uses a continuous-time deep ODE variational model to learn and forecast supernova light curves, delivering millisecond-scale inference for thousands of objects—replacing slow MCMC pipelines with a fast, amortized approach.
problem_solved: How to perform accurate, uncertainty-aware inference and forecasting on irregularly sampled, high-volume transient light curves at Rubin/LSST scale (≈10M alerts/night) when traditional physics-based MCMC methods are too slow to keep up.
method: Continuous-time variational autoencoder built with Neural ODEs: encoder maps observations to a latent ODE state, latent dynamics are governed by a learned ODE, decoder reconstructs light curves and physical parameters.
Amortized inference for rapid posterior estimation and forecasting on irregularly sampled time series, with built-in uncertainty quantification (probabilistic decoder/latent posterior).
Training on simulated/observed supernova light curves to learn physical evolution and enable millisecond-scale inference for large alert streams.
impact: Enables real-time, scalable classification and parameter estimation for astronomical transients—allowing prioritized follow-up and rapid scientific discovery at survey scale while preserving uncertainty estimates. Practitioners get a template for applying Neural ODE VAEs to other irregular, high-throughput time-series problems.
visual_elements: Model diagram: encoder → latent Neural ODE (continuous trajectory) → decoder, showing amortized inference and sampling

paper_title: SELDON: Supernova Explosions Learned by Deep ODE Networks
paper_authors: Jiezhong Wu, Jack O'Brien, Jennifer Li, M. S. Krafczyk, Ved G. Shah
